text: Cytosolic DNA acts as a danger signal that triggers type I interferon responses in mammalian cells. DNA induces interferons via cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP), which binds and activates the adaptor protein STING. Using biochemical fractionation and quantitative mass spectrometry, researchers identified cGAMP synthase (cGAS), a member of the nucleotidyltransferase family. cGAS overexpression activated transcription factor IRF3 and induced interferon-β in a STING-dependent manner. Conversely, cGAS knockdown inhibited IRF3 activation and interferon-β induction following DNA transfection or DNA virus infection. cGAS bound DNA in the cytoplasm and catalyzed cGAMP synthesis. These findings indicate that cGAS is a cytosolic DNA sensor that induces interferons by producing the second messenger cGAMP.
